name: Milk Thistle
title: Milk Thistle | The Hippie Scientist
description: Milk thistle (Silybum marianum) is a spiny plant whose seeds yield silymarin, a mixture of flavonolignans with antioxidant activity. Although it is best known as a 'liver tonic,' rigorous evidence for liver disease is limited and inconclusive; its clearer signal is metabolic. A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials in type 2 diabetes found that silymarin reduced fasting blood glucose and HbA1c compared with control, while not significantly changing blood lipids. The included trials were few and small, so larger studies are needed. Milk thistle is generally well tolerated.

name: Pomegranate
title: Pomegranate | The Hippie Scientist
description: Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit whose juice and peel are rich in punicalagins and other polyphenols with antioxidant activity. Its best-studied cardiovascular effect is on blood pressure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found that drinking pomegranate juice modestly lowered both systolic and diastolic blood pressure, an effect seen across different doses and study durations. Pomegranate can inhibit drug-metabolizing enzymes, so, like grapefruit, it may interact with some medications; anyone taking prescription drugs regularly should check with a pharmacist.

name: Psyllium
title: Psyllium | The Hippie Scientist
description: Psyllium is the soluble fiber from the husks of Plantago ovata seeds, best known as a bulk-forming laxative. Because it forms a viscous gel that binds bile acids, it also affects blood lipids: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found that psyllium supplementation lowered LDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B versus control, with roughly 10 grams per day a commonly studied dose. Psyllium should be taken with ample water and separated in time from other medications, whose absorption its gel can slow.

name: Saw Palmetto (Serenoa repens)
title: Saw Palmetto (Serenoa repens) | The Hippie Scientist
description: Saw palmetto (Serenoa repens) is a dwarf palm whose berry extract, rich in fatty acids and phytosterols, is one of the most widely sold supplements for prostate and urinary symptoms. The best available evidence does not support that use: in the CAMUS randomized trial, saw palmetto extract escalated to double and triple the usual 320 mg daily dose did not reduce lower urinary tract symptoms more than placebo. It is generally well tolerated, but men with urinary symptoms should be evaluated by a clinician rather than self-treating.

Its primary lignans (schisandrin A/B/C) support hepatocyte detoxification via CYP450 modulation and exhibit antioxidant activity. Human data support mild stress reduction and liver enzyme normalization in hepatitis populations.

description: Saw palmetto (Serenoa repens) is a dwarf palm whose berry extract, rich in fatty acids and phytosterols, is widely sold for prostate symptoms. Despite its popularity, the evidence does not support it: a large Cochrane systematic review found that saw palmetto, even at double and triple the usual dose, did not improve urinary flow, night-time urination, or overall symptoms of benign prostatic enlargement compared with placebo. It is generally well tolerated, but men with urinary symptoms should be evaluated by a clinician rather than relying on it.
